- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — add 1–3% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.25) and price is trending upward, model lags — forecast should be 1–2% higher than historical mean for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is flat and price is trending downward, model overestimates — forecast should be 1–2% lower than historical mean for next 5 days.  
- Model ignores sentiment when price is near 70–75 range — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment if sentiment shifts >0.3 in 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 76.67 → 70.52), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral.
